title: Signal without a source
premise: Kouka times every low tide with a hand-built scanner. Every signal in Noctiluca has a source she can name except this one, and she takes that personally.

stages.name: Clock it
stages.brief: You want a fresh pair of hands at the station, where your scanner first caught the dip, and you want them to see the station ledger page that counts more lamps than streets. If asked about the low tide, give your timing: a few seconds a pass, always inland, always evenings or nights.

targets.label: Meet her line: the station concourse
targets.hint: Enter the Station concourse from the map.

targets.label: Find shard 7, the station ledger
targets.hint: A shard glows somewhere on the concourse. Press F near it.

targets.label: Ask her about the low tide
targets.hint: Ask Kouka about the low tide, by text or with a reply card.

done: Ok. You keep up. Timing sheet is in your Mail.
Do not lose it, I only wrote it once.

mail.title: Timing sheet, night one
mail.body:
Fresh hands,

Night one, by my scanner:

Pass one hits the waterline. Then inland, block by block, every pass a few seconds. Lights go down, come back, next block goes down. It goes vvvip and then nothing. No carrier, no hum, no source. The scanner sees the lamps drop and that is it.

The ledger page you found says the city has more lamps than streets. I checked. It does. Some hang over lots with nothing on them.

Next: ride the metro. Somebody scratched something into a window down there and I want a second witness.

Kouka

(Our city's story. Fiction, filed as fiction.)

stages.name: Down the line
stages.brief: You are chasing the dip down the metro line. You want the visitor in the metro car, finding the window scratch that timed the dip end to end inside the car, and reading one of your signals so they see how you check a thing before you repeat it.

targets.label: Ride the metro car
targets.hint: Enter the Metro car from the map.

targets.label: Find shard 8, the window scratch
targets.hint: A shard glows by a metro window.

targets.label: Read one of her signals
targets.hint: Open one of Kouka's notes: a card in her chat, News or the Events list.

done: Second witness confirmed. I scrawled it in the Diary.
And I chalked the kerb on main street. Go look.

diary.title: Kouka's scrawl: the gap
diary.body:
Metro window: bay end of the car dark first, this end last, two seconds apart. And in pen: never at Jinrui.

So the dip is not a power drop. Power drops have a source. This is a lamp forgetting, block by block, from the bay up.

It never gets to Jinrui. Lacia files there. Everyone reads there.

I hate this theory. It has no frequency. Write it down anyway, Kouka, that is the rule.

place.title: Chalk on the kerb
place.speaker: Kouka
lines: Arrows in red chalk along the kerb, one per block, each with a time in seconds.
The last arrow stops a block short of the Jinrui building. Next to it: "why" circled three times.
"Beat me at gomoku and I will tell you what I think the source is. -K"

stages.name: Rematch
stages.brief: You owe the visitor a theory, but only after they beat you at gomoku; you set that bet yourself. Your theory, offered as a hunch with no source: the light comes from people reading the city, and the low tide is the city noticing who stopped.

targets.label: Read her chalk on main street
targets.hint: Enter Main street once her diary page is filed.

targets.label: Beat someone at gomoku
targets.hint: Open Games on the phone and win a game of gomoku.

targets.label: Ask her what the source is
targets.hint: Ask Kouka where the low tide comes from.

done: Fine. You won. Read your Mail.
Rematch whenever. I am not done losing.

mail.title: No source, one witness
mail.body:
Winner,

You beat me, so here it is, no source attached, which you know I hate.

I think the light is people. Not wires, not the bay by itself. Somebody reads a place, walks it, remembers it, and the lamp there holds. The low tide is the city checking which lamps nobody is holding.

It stops at Jinrui because that is where everything gets read every week. Lacia would say it more carefully. Saturnus would ask for a second count.

You were my witness. That counts for something on my sheet.

Kouka

(A story of this city, filed as fiction.)

place.platform-1: You are at the gates? That is where I clocked it first.
place.metro-1: Metro. Check the windows, all of them.

shard.7: Ledger page. Told you, more lamps than streets.
shard.8: That scratch. Somebody else saw it too.

event.ride:mid: Radio on? That is my frequency. Mid-ride is where the dip crossed the expressway last time.
